title: Adaptive Prometheus scrape configurator and dashboard pruner for private installs
author: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Add an adaptive Prometheus scrape-configurator component and a dashboard-pruner job to the private-installer to reduce memory and scrape overhead for multi-tenant private clusters. Motivation: Large private installs were suffering from excessive scrape cardinality and stale tenant dashboards accumulating in Grafana which increased memory and UI clutter. This PR introduces an operator-style reconciler that watches tenant labels and workload hints to generate targeted scrape_configs and a periodic pruner that removes dashboards older than a configurable TTL unless pinned. Goals include: 1) reduce Prometheus scrape_count spikes during churn, 2) keep Grafana folders manageable, 3) provide safe rollback and opt-out via installer flags. Implementation: terraform module exposes new optional values: observability.adaptive_scrape.enabled, scrape.hints.namespace_selector, dashboard_pruner.enabled and dashboard_pruner.ttl_days. Helm chart adds a new subchart prometheus-adaptive-scraper with two Deployments: scraper-controller (rbac, CRD-lite) and scraper-syncer (batch sync with leader-election). The chart also adds a CronJob grafana-dashboard-pruner that calls our internal api to mark/delete dashboards and emits audit events to stdout for log-shipper consumption. The reconciler builds scrape_configs on runtime annotations and tenant prometheusRule hints. It writes to a mounted ConfigMap which Prometheus picks up via a file_sd target; the installer adds an init-hook to migrate existing static scrape_configs to the new format during upgrade. Rollback/upgrade: all changes are feature-flag guarded and the helm templates include a migration-hook that can be skipped. We included a toggle to keep both old and new configs for one release window and an automated rollback playbook in docs. Testing: unit tests for reconciler logic, integration test harness that brings up a scaled-down Prometheus+Grafana using the private-installer k3s profile, and a simulated tenant churn test showing scrape reduction of ~37% in our synthetic workloads. Security: RBAC limited to observability namespace and serviceAccount token rotation supported via existing KMS integration. Backward compatibility: defaults keep the feature disabled; upgrade path documented. Related: ENG-4215 for cost reductions, ENG-4360 for dashboard hygiene. Checklist: add terraform variables, helm templates, reconciler binary, tests, docs, and migration notes.

review_comments: Luca Moretti: Can we avoid writing directly to ConfigMap to prevent excessive etcd churn? Suggest writing to a shared file volume and letting a small sidecar update the ConfigMap on a slow cadence. Response (Aisha): Implemented file_sd writer to a hostPath-backed volume with a short-lived sidecar to update configmaps only if the checksum changed. See cmd/scraper-reconciler/main.go commit c7d1f2a.

Priya Sharma: The CronJob could cause race with manual dashboard edits. Can we add a pin label to protect dashboards? Response (Aisha): Yes, pruner now checks for grafana_labels: pinned=true and skips deletion. Added tests to cover pin behavior.

Ben Turner: Add metrics for pruner actions and scraper reconciliation duration. Response (Aisha): Added Prometheus metrics namespaced under redwood_private_installer_adaptive_scrape_{reconcile_duration_seconds,applied_configs_total,skipped_configs_total} and dashboard_pruner_{deleted_total,skipped_pinned_total}.

Security review (Kelsey Reed): Confirmed RBAC scope limited to observability namespace and pruner uses readonly Grafana API token for listing dashboards and a deletion token stored in secret. Response (Aisha): documented token rotation and key usage.
release_notes: Added an opt-in adaptive Prometheus scrape configurator to reduce scrape cardinality and a Grafana dashboard pruner CronJob to clean up unpinned dashboards. Feature disabled by default; enable with observability.adaptive_scrape.enabled=true. Includes migration hook and rollback playbook.
notes_for_operators: Default: feature disabled. To enable in an existing private install: set terraform variable observability.adaptive_scrape.enabled=true and apply. Review the migration log at /var/log/installer/migrate-scrape-configs.log. To roll back: run helm upgrade with adaptive_scrape.enabled=false and follow docs/private-observability/rollback-playbook.md. Monitor metrics under redwood_private_installer_adaptive_scrape_*.
